title: useEffect — and when not to use it

questions.prompt: Which of these genuinely needs a useEffect?

options.text: Computing a user's full name from first + last name
Filtering a list based on a search box value
Subscribing to a WebSocket and updating when messages arrive

questions.explanation: Effects synchronize with systems OUTSIDE React — subscriptions, timers, the DOM, the network. Full name, filtering, and date formatting are all derived during render; doing them in an Effect adds a render and can desync. Only the WebSocket reaches an external system.

questions.prompt: What does the dependency array [roomId] actually promise React?

options.text: Re-run this effect (after cleaning up the previous one) whenever roomId changes
Run the effect only one time, ever
Memoize roomId so it never changes
Debounce the effect until roomId stops changing

questions.explanation: The dependency array is a claim about WHEN to re-synchronize: clean up with the previous values, then re-run with the new ones, whenever a listed value changes. [] means 'never re-run' (sync once); omitting the array entirely means 'run after every render'.

prompts.prompt: Complete the subscription effect: subscribe on mount, re-subscribe when roomId changes, and clean up to avoid leaks.
prompts.explanation: The cleanup tears down the old connection before the next run (and on unmount). Listing roomId re-runs the effect — disconnect old, connect new — on every room change. Omit the cleanup and you leak one connection per switch.

snippets.question: What value does the counter show after ~5 seconds, and why?
snippets.explanation: Empty deps → the effect runs once and closes over count = 0 forever (a stale closure). Every tick computes 0 + 1 = 1. Fix with the functional updater setCount(c => c + 1), which always reads the latest value and needs no count in the deps.

snippets.question: What is logged on the first render, then after one click?
snippets.explanation: React runs render first (logs 'render n'), commits to the DOM, then runs effects (logs 'effect n') — effects fire AFTER paint, and with no dependency array, after every render. So 'render' always logs before 'effect', each time n changes.
